response.sql:
WITH fee_orders AS (
  SELECT f.feesnode, f.feerate, f.rebrate, f.orderslink, o.dealedge
  FROM fees f
  INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009
),
group_stats AS (
  SELECT orderslink, dealedge, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS group_avg_net_fee, COUNT(*) AS group_count
  FROM fee_orders
  GROUP BY orderslink, dealedge
),
side_avgs AS (
  SELECT dealedge, AVG(group_avg_net_fee) AS side_avg_net_fee
  FROM group_stats
  GROUP BY dealedge
)
SELECT gs.orderslink, gs.dealedge, gs.group_avg_net_fee, gs.group_count, gs.group_avg_net_fee - sa.side_avg_net_fee AS diff
FROM group_stats gs
JOIN side_avgs sa ON gs.dealedge = sa.dealedge
WHERE gs.group_avg_net_fee > sa.side_avg_net_fee
ORDER BY diff DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: "Number of records" refers to COUNT(*) for all records in each (orderslink, dealedge) group, including those with NULL rebrate. The phrase "ignoring missing values" applies specifically to the average net fee rate calculation, where SQL's AVG() function naturally skips NULL values during aggregation.

alternatives.interpretation: "Number of records" refers only to records with non-NULL rebrate values, such that both the count and average exclude fees lacking a rebate rate.
